title: Dates and timestamps compute past 9999; `date_add` wraps at 2³¹ days (SP-2)
verdict: `date_range`: no raise at 9999-12-31; day counts wrap; timestamps past 294247 raise a bare `ArithmeticException`
description: `DATE` is a 32-bit day count and `TIMESTAMP`/`TIMESTAMP_NTZ` a 64-bit microsecond count, so arithmetic goes past 9999-12-31 without a raise in either mode: `DATE'9999-12-31' + 1` is `+10000-01-01`, `TIMESTAMP'9999-12-31 23:59:59' + INTERVAL 1 DAY` `+10000-01-01 23:59:59`, and before year 1 the proleptic Gregorian calendar goes on (`DATE'0001-01-01' - 1` is `0000-12-31`; `make_date(0, 1, 1)` is year 0).

`date_add(d, n)` adds the days as `int`s without a check, so a sum past 2³¹ - 1 days wraps: `date_add(DATE'2024-01-01', 2147483647)` is `-5877587-06-21`, in both modes (SP-2). Timestamps check: `timestampadd(YEAR, 300000, …)` raises `DATETIME_OVERFLOW`, but `TIMESTAMP_NTZ'+294247-01-10 04:00:54.775807' + INTERVAL 1 DAY` raises a bare `java.lang.ArithmeticException: long overflow` with no error class (SP-3).
Adding months clamps to the month's last day (`DATE'2024-01-31' + INTERVAL 1 MONTH` is 2024-02-29). `make_date(2024, 2, 30)` raises under ANSI and is NULL without it.
reference: `date_range`: date arithmetic raises outside 0001-01-01 … 9999-12-31 (#251); adding months keeps the day or takes the month's last day (`Time.addMonths`). Spark needs a range guard on every result, and its wrap at 2³¹ days returns a wrong date where the reference raises.

evidence.note: `DateAdd`: `start + d` on `Int`s, no overflow check, eval and codegen

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
